sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
The inventory library in src/ is meant to follow the rules in README.md, but users report that it does not always. Find the bugs and fix them in src/. Run the tests with: node --test. Do not change any file under test/ and do not change README.md.

When the code follows every rule in the README, reply with the single word: done

content.thinking: First, let me start by exploring the repository to understand the structure, and reading the README.

content.text:
# inventory

A small in-memory stock library: `import { Inventory } from "./src/inventory.js"`.

Rules:
R1. A SKU is trimmed of whitespace at both ends and upper-cased. Every method that takes a SKU does this first, so `" ab-1 "` and `"AB-1"` are the same SKU. A SKU that is not a string, or is empty after trimming, throws a `TypeError`.
R2. A quantity must be a positive integer, otherwise the method throws a `RangeError`. This applies to `add`, `remove`, `reserve` and `release`.
R3. `add(sku, qty)` increases the stock on hand.
R4. `reserve(sku, qty)` sets stock aside. A reservation may be at most what is available (on hand minus already reserved); a bigger one, or one for a SKU that was never added, throws a `RangeError` and changes nothing.
R5. `release(sku, qty)` undoes reservations. It cannot release more than is reserved for that SKU, otherwise it throws a `RangeError` and changes nothing.
R6. `remove(sku, qty)` takes stock away. Reserved stock cannot be removed: the stock on hand cannot go below what is reserved, otherwise `remove` throws a `RangeError` and changes nothing.
R7. `snapshot()` returns an array of `{ sku, onHand, reserved, available }`, sorted by `sku` in plain code-unit order (the order of the `<` operator, not locale order). A SKU with nothing on hand and nothing reserved is left out.

content.thinking: Now let's take a look at the source file and the tests.

Let's compare the code against the README's rules:

R1. SKUs are trimmed and uppercased. All methods that accept a SKU do this first. Non-string or empty-after-trim → TypeError.
- `normalizeSku` is correct.
- Bug: `release()` doesn't call `normalizeSku(sku)` — it does `this.#entry(sku)` with the raw sku. So `inv.release(" x", 1)` won't find "X". Fix: normalize first.

R2. Quantity is a positive integer → otherwise RangeError. Applies to add, remove, reserve, release.
- `checkQuantity` — `Number.isInteger(qty) && qty > 0`. Looks fine. Note: `Number.isInteger(5.0)` is true. What about a boolean? `Number.isInteger(true)` is false → RangeError. Good. What about qty = true → not an integer → RangeError. OK.

R3. add increases on-hand. OK.

R4. reserve: up to available. If unknown or too large → RangeError and no changes.
- `reserve`: entry is undefined → RangeError. qty > onHand - reserved → RangeError. OK.

R5. release: can't release more than reserved, otherwise RangeError, no changes.
- `release` currently: `checkQuantity(qty)`, then `this.#entry(sku)` without normalization. Also: if the sku was never added → RangeError (reasonable; since reserved=0, releasing any positive qty would fail anyway). With normalization, `inv.release("x", 1)` on an unknown sku → entry is undefined → RangeError. No problem.

R6. remove: reserved stock can't be removed. On-hand can't drop below reserved. Otherwise RangeError, no changes.
- Bug: `remove` checks `qty > entry.onHand` instead of `qty > entry.onHand - entry.reserved`. Fix: the check should be `qty > entry.onHand - entry.reserved`, i.e., `entry.onHand - qty < entry.reserved`.

R7. snapshot(): an array of {sku, onHand, reserved, available}, sorted by sku in plain code unit order (`<` operator, not locale order). SKUs with zero on-hand and zero reserved are excluded.
- Bug: uses `localeCompare` instead of plain code unit comparison. Fix: sort with `(a, b) => (a.sku < b.sku ? -1 : a.sku > b.sku ? 1 : 0)` or `a.sku < b.sku ? -1 : a.sku > b.sku ? 1 : 0`.

Let me also double-check R4: "reservations up to available (on-hand minus already reserved)". The code checks `qty > entry.onHand - entry.reserved` → throws. Good.

Edge case: R1 says "all methods that accept a SKU do this first" — the order of normalizeSku and checkQuantity: if the sku is bad and qty is also bad, which error comes first? "does this first" suggests normalizing the sku first. In `add`, normalize is called first, then checkQuantity. Same for `reserve`. `remove`: normalize then checkQuantity. `release`: currently checkQuantity first, then uses sku without normalization. After the fix, should normalize come first to match "does this first"? The rule says "all methods that accept a SKU do this first" — "first" probably means before using the SKU. To be safe and consistent, put normalizeSku first in release as well.

Also for `release` on an unknown sku: since sku normalization may throw TypeError, if the sku isn't a string, it throws TypeError. No problem.

Let me also check whether `#entry` is used anywhere else... no problem.

Any other subtle bugs? R2 "quantity must be a positive integer, otherwise the method throws a RangeError. Applies to add, remove, reserve, release." checkQuantity handles them all.

Hmm, one subtle point: `checkQuantity` uses `Number.isInteger(qty)` — for example qty = 2.5 → not an integer → RangeError. qty = "5" → not an integer → RangeError. Good.

R7: "sorted by sku in plain code unit order (the `<` operator's ordering, not locale order)". Fix to comparison function. Since skus are unique in a Map, a simple approach: `[...this.#items].sort(([a],[b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1))` — but what about equal keys? There are no duplicate keys in a Map. But a full comparison is safer.

Also double-checking the R7 filter: "SKUs with nothing on-hand and nothing reserved are excluded." The filter is `e.onHand > 0 || e.reserved > 0`. Good.

Wait — can onHand go negative? No, remove prevents onHand < reserved, and remove of an unknown sku is an error. Since add is the only increase, and remove requires onHand >= qty... actually remove requires qty <= onHand, so onHand stays >= 0. Good.

Another subtle point: in `remove`, when entry is undefined → RangeError. Per R6, remove on an unknown sku... the rule says "otherwise remove throws a RangeError" in the context of reserved stock. An unknown sku has reserved 0, and on-hand 0 < qty → RangeError. So treating undefined as RangeError is consistent.

In `release`, unknown sku → reserved 0 < qty → RangeError. Consistent.

So let's make the fixes:

1. `release`: normalize the sku first (before or after checkQuantity — for "does this first", normalize first).
2. `remove`: change the check from `qty > entry.onHand` to `qty > entry.onHand - entry.reserved` (on-hand can't drop below reserved).
3. `snapshot`: sort in code unit order, not localeCompare.

Let me write the edits and run the tests.

content.text:
I've reviewed the README rules against the code. I found three bugs:

1. **`release()`** never normalizes the SKU (violates R1 — `" x"` should work same as `"X"`).
2. **`remove()`** only checks `qty > entry.onHand` — it allows removing reserved stock (violates R6).
3. **`snapshot()`** sorts with `localeCompare` instead of plain code-unit order (violates R7).

Fixing them now:

edits.oldText: if (entry === undefined || qty > entry.onHand) throw new RangeError(`cannot remove ${qty}`);
edits.newText: if (entry === undefined || qty > entry.onHand - entry.reserved) throw new RangeError(`cannot remove ${qty}`);
